title: L-BFGS-B Optimized Three-Cavity Filter with QWOT-Seeded Initialization
scientific_hypothesis: Curvature-aware L-BFGS-B optimization with Hessian approximation, initialized at ±20% jittered quarter-wave optical thickness estimates, will navigate flat-gradient regions near resonance peaks more effectively than gradient descent, yielding higher target scores and improved robustness margins for the three-cavity Ge/ZnS topology.
design_principle: Multi-cavity Fabry-Perot bandpass filter with computational optimization using second-order information for step sizing in thickness space
proposed_topology: 21-layer alternating Ge/ZnS stack on CaF2 substrate: Air|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|CaF2
manufacturing_considerations: thickness bounds 50-500 nm for deposition control
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory for Fabry-Perot cavity formation
L-BFGS-B optimization with Hessian approximation for non-convex thickness spaces
expected_advantages: Better convergence in flat-gradient regions near resonance
Higher target scores than gradient descent baseline
known_risks: L-BFGS-B may converge to different local minima than gradient descent
execution_request_english: Design a 21-layer alternating Ge/ZnS dielectric bandpass filter on CaF2 substrate for normal incidence. Layer sequence: Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge (21 finite layers). Initialize all layer thicknesses using quarter-wave optical thickness estimates at 4.45 μm center wavelength with ±20% uniform random jitter, bounded to 50-500 nm per layer. Optimize using L-BFGS-B algorithm with Hessian approximation enabled. Evaluate transmittance at four wavelength bands: maximize in 4150-4350 nm and 4550-4750 nm, minimize in 3600-4000 nm and 4850-5200 nm. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
revision_reason: Changed optimizer from gradient descent to L-BFGS-B with Hessian approximation and reinitialized thicknesses with ±20% QWOT jitter per feedback directive to explore adjacent harmonic basins with curvature-aware step sizing
